name: Little Elm
seo_title: Little Elm Christmas Events: Parade, Circus, Santa 2026
seo_description: A Merry Little Elm Christmas parade and tree lighting Dec 5, Breakfast with Santa and Grinchmas at The Cove, and Do Portugal Circus Dec 11 to 27.
lede: The story of Christmas in Little Elm starts with Kit King, who founded the community on the banks of Little Elm Creek in 1844. In 2025 the town merged its tree lighting and Christmas parade into one free night, A Merry Little Elm Christmas, on The Lawn in the Lakefront District.
sections: The Handbook of Texas says Little Elm was established in 1844 by Kit King on the banks of Little Elm Creek. The county's first post office opened in King's house in 1852, and King's Crossing was used by the stagecoach from Preston Bend to Bird's Fort. The first store opened in 1859. In 1866 Henry Hill built a store a mile east and the post office moved there as Hilltown. Little Elm had 194 people in 1900, 363 by 1976, when it had incorporated, and 3,646 in 2000.
One new Christmas night on the Lakefront

In November 2025 the Town of Little Elm announced a brand new celebration, A Merry Little Elm Christmas, on Saturday, December 6, 2025, at The Lawn in The Lakefront District. The Town said it was uniting its tree lighting and Christmas parade into one free event, with a parade route from the Brenda Button Mills Senior Center down Main Street to near The Cove, then a tree lighting, a surprise show and a Frozen screening. The 2026 edition is Saturday, December 5, from 5 to 9 pm, with The Grinch (2018) as the movie.

The Town's motto is The Town with a Lake Attitude, and its Lewisville Lake shoreline runs more than 66 miles, but DCTA's A-train station list has no Little Elm stop. Its stations are in Denton, Lewisville and Carrollton. On Saturday, December 5, 2026, DCTA runs Santa at the Station from the Downtown Denton Transit Center, the same day as the Little Elm parade. For a longer train day, the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco and the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano are a drive away.

faq: How did Little Elm get its start?

The Handbook of Texas says Kit King established Little Elm in 1844 on the banks of Little Elm Creek. Its first post office, the first in Denton County, opened in King's house in 1852, and King's Crossing served the stagecoach between Preston Bend and Bird's Fort. The town had incorporated by 1976, when it counted 363 residents.
When and where is the Little Elm tree lighting in 2026?

A Merry Little Elm Christmas is Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 5 to 9 pm at The Lawn at The Lakefront, 125 Main Street. Discover Little Elm lists the cost as free. The parade is listed at 6:45 pm, the tree lighting at 7:30 pm and The Grinch movie at 7:35 pm, with Santa photos after the lighting.
Is there a Christmas parade in Little Elm?

Yes. In 2025 the Town combined its tree lighting and Christmas parade into A Merry Little Elm Christmas. That year the route began at the Brenda Button Mills Senior Center, ran down Main Street at The Lawn and ended near The Cove. Discover Little Elm lists the 2026 parade as part of the same free Lakefront night.
What is the Christmas circus in Little Elm?

Do Portugal Circus brings A Night Before Christmas to Little Elm Park, 701 W Eldorado Parkway, from December 11 to 27, 2026. The show has aerial acts, acrobatics, high-wire acts and dancers under the big top. The circus ticket page lists prices from $15 to $50, and Discover Little Elm shows $15 to $35.
What is The Lakefront in Little Elm?

The Lakefront District is the heart of Little Elm's events, with The Lawn on Main Street, restaurants, a beach and The Cove waterpark. The Town says its Lakefront restaurants and businesses add giveaways, holiday drinks and snacks around the Christmas parade night, and it calls the town The Town with a Lake Attitude.
Can we take a train to Little Elm?

DCTA's A-train does not list a stop in Little Elm. For a Christmas train ride, DCTA runs Santa at the Station on Saturday, December 5, 2026, from the Downtown Denton Transit Center. The Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco is another train stop for the family.
